revise_description: In the stakeholder handoff for this case, the finance partner framed the change in business terms rather than as a spreadsheet checklist. The commercial owner described the rule as a gate, not a smooth surcharge. Crossing a named business line changes eligibility for the allowance, desk, setup, waiver, or fee; staying on the other side does not. The product team wants A1 to remain available for a priority customer program, but the equipment group warned that crossing the usual A1 comfort band changes the month rather than simply raising unit volume. Once A1 clears `a1_watch_threshold`, the plant must book the quality-release crew, pay `a1_quality_release_fee`, and give up `maintenance_penalty_watch` operating day. If A1 clears the deeper service level `a1_deep_service_threshold`, a second teardown day is lost and `a1_deep_service_fee` is charged. Only A1 units above the first watch level receive the priority uplift `a1_priority_price_lift`; all product lines still have to be run at commercially meaningful batch sizes. The names shown in backticks are the exact field names used by the data packet and the audit trail.
